method: World Athletics Technical Rules fix the landing sector at 34.92 degrees for the shot put, discus and hammer and at 28.96 degrees for the javelin, measured between the inner edges of two lines that, if extended, meet at the centre of the throwing circle or, for the javelin, at the centre of the foul arc 8 m behind it. The tool takes the event, a distance out along one sector line and the unit, then works from that apex: the cross distance between the ends of the two equal lines is 2 x r x sin(theta / 2), half of it is r x sin(theta / 2), the arc at that distance is r x theta and the landing area inside it is 0.5 x r^2 x theta, with theta the full sector angle in radians. For 34.92 degrees the ratio 2 x sin(17.46 degrees) is 0.60008, so the rule-book shortcut of 0.60 times the line length (12 m across at 20 m, 48 m at 80 m, 60 m at 100 m) agrees to within 0.02 per cent; for 28.96 degrees the ratio 2 x sin(14.48 degrees) is 0.50008, which is 50 m across at 100 m from the arc centre. Because a javelin throw is measured from the throwing arc, the tape runs from the arc centre at the entered distance plus the 8 m arc radius, and the page reports that radial distance alongside the entered one. A sector 0.1 degrees too wide, the USATF rule 187.22 allowance, moves the cross distance by 2 x r x (sin((theta + 0.1) / 2) - sin(theta / 2)), which is 2.0 in at a 100 ft line. Distances are accepted from 1 to 120 m or 3 to 400 ft; the unit scales every length linearly and leaves the angles unchanged, and the table steps through 10 m or 25 ft from one step to ten. The core rounds its lengths and areas to five decimal places and the page shows two, so a 34.92 degree sector reads 12.00 m across at 20 m rather than the exact 12.0016 m. This is marking arithmetic only: it assumes level ground and a sector centred on the throwing direction, it does not survey a site, set competition markings or replace the competition's own field regulations, and laying a sector out still needs a tape, pegs and a second pair of hands. Everything runs in the browser; nothing is sent, stored or uploaded.

sources.title: PNTF officials guide, Laying Out Sector Angles for the Track & Field Throwing Events (rev.
